thread:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert - ELB target health count dropped in us-west-2 for service/redwood-inference-api (automated)
Maya Patel: Got the page, on it. Pulling up ELB and Route53 now.
Raj Singh: I'm nearby, looking at CloudWatch 5xx spike and ELB unhealthy hosts. Any customer impact reported yet?
Claire Brooks: Support sees a spike in 502/504 from multiple customers in us-west-2. A few high-traffic tenants reporting errors. No internal outage page yet.
Priya Desai: Observation: ELB target group tg-abc has many hosts in draining/unhealthy. Metrics show deregistration spikes and connection resets. Could be AZ networking flap.
Tom Nguyen: Confirming: EC2 & EBS API errors in us-west-2 in recent 10m from AWS status. Route53 health checks show intermittent failures for our origin endpoints.
Maya Patel: Ok, action plan: 1) Pause deployments to us-west-2 2) Initiate failover routing for critical routes to us-west-1 3) Scale up dedicated pool in us-west-1 for traffic shift
Raj Singh: I can flip the weighted routing policy for the customer-facing record to 0.8 -> us-west-1 and 0.2 -> us-west-2 as a staged failover.
Priya Desai: Can someone run a quick curl against the ELB to reproduce 502? Logs attached here (snip):

```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/health
* Connected to elb-usw2-123.amazonaws.com
< HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
```

Tom Nguyen: Also seeing elevated TCP retransmits in us-west-2 AZ-a. Might be a networking plane partial loss.
Maya Patel: ops-pager: please escalate to AWS support (sev1) and create a ticket referencing ELB/EC2/EBS impact in us-west-2.
ops-pager: Pager acknowledged, opening AWS support case now. ETA 15-30m.
Claire Brooks: Noting customers impacted: Acme, NovaApps, and two PLG self-serve orgs. Support working on status updates.
Raj Singh: Executing Route53 weighted update now:

```
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z123 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"api.redwood.example.com","Type":"A","SetIdentifier":"us-west-1","Weight":80,"AliasTarget":{"HostedZoneId":"ZALIAS","DNSName":"elb-usw1-999.amazonaws.com","EvaluateTargetHealth":true}}]}}'
```

Maya Patel: After flip, monitoring for error rate and latency.
Priya Desai: Post-switch check: traffic to us-west-1 increased as expected, 5xx rate dropped 60% overall.
Tom Nguyen: Still seeing some residual errors hitting us-west-2 origin. We'll keep a low weight on us-west-2 until AWS confirms stability.
Claire Brooks: Sending customer comms draft to SRE-runbook channel for review. Want to mention partial regional impact and failover in place.
Maya Patel: Good. Also add "we are investigating root cause with AWS; traffic has been routed to an alternate region to reduce customer impact." Keep it short.
Raj Singh: FYI I increased ELB connection timeout on healthy targets to reduce flapping: changed deregistration delay to 120s on tg-abc.
Priya Desai: Noted. Also toggled auto-scaler to prefer us-west-1 nodes for the next 30m.
ops-pager: AWS support responded: "Investigating networking connectivity in us-west-2; we are seeing elevated API error rates." Case ID: 987654321.
Tom Nguyen: Can we enable cross-region read replicas for any stateful components hit by AZ connectivity? If not immediate, ensure we don't trigger writes that depend on those hosts.
Maya Patel: For now, enable read-only fallback where possible and increase retry/backoff on write paths for affected customers.
Claire Brooks: Customer updates sent: initial notice in 10m, follow-up scheduled in 30m. Added affected customer list and mitigation steps.
Raj Singh: Monitoring: configured synthetic canaries to hit the new us-west-1 endpoint and validated responses. No 5xx at 5m post-switchover.
Priya Desai: Will capture logs for postmortem: ELB metrics, target group events, ASG scale events, Route53 change history, AWS status timeline.
Maya Patel: Handing off to Raj for night shift. Raj, please continue monitoring and update the incident channel every 30m until resolved.
Raj Singh: Taking over. Summary for next on-call: regional us-west-2 ELB/EC2/EBS anomalies causing target flapping and 5xxs; traffic weighted to us-west-1; AWS case open 987654321. I'll trigger full postmortem once AWS provides RCA.
Priya Desai: Quick note — disable non-critical background jobs hitting storage in us-west-2 to reduce load while degraded.
ops-pager: AWS updated: "We have recovered some control plane components in us-west-2; customers may see gradual improvement. Continue monitoring."
Tom Nguyen: Observed healthy host counts gradually returning in AZ-b, AZ-c. Keep low weight until stable for 1 hour.
Claire Brooks: Marking incident severity: P1 -> customer-facing errors affecting multiple tenants. Postmortem lead: Priya. SLA impact: potential partial degradation for some paid customers; billing/credits TBD.
Maya Patel: Closing loop: once us-west-2 healthy hosts >= 95% and 5xx baseline back to < 5/min for 60m, we can start shifting traffic back.
Raj Singh: 1h check: metrics look stable. Plan to move 50% back to us-west-2 and observe for 30m.
Priya Desai: Make sure to annotate all config changes and Route53 history in the incident doc for audit.
Maya Patel: Thanks team. Good triage and quick failover. We'll run a short retro tomorrow to tighten our runbooks for cross-region failovers. :thumbsup:
incident-bot: Incident declared resolved in channel incident-status. Root cause pending AWS RCA. Postmortem scheduled: /calendar invite sent to SRE, Eng-Platform, Support.
